_comment: 10 diverse mock student profiles. Grades are on 0-20 (math, algorithmics, programming, networks); skills on 0-10 (problem_solving, coding_practice); interests on 0-10 per major (ai, se, cyber). A null 'interests' object means the interest questionnaire was NOT filled (missing data). S07 carries a second questionnaire ('interests_followup') used by the belief-revision demonstration. Each 'role' field documents which reasoning phenomenon the profile is designed to exhibit.

students.name: Amina Belkacem
students.role: Clear AI talent; also administratively eligible for SE; declared dislike of cybersecurity blocks the cyber default.

students.name: Yacine Haddad
students.role: Clear software-engineering profile (strong programmer, weak in networks).

students.name: Meriem Saadi
students.role: Clear cybersecurity profile; declared dislikes of AI and SE defeat those defaults even if grades rose.

students.name: Sofiane Meziane
students.role: Weak overall record (average < 10): no major is accessible; all three methods must agree on remediation.

students.name: Lina Zerouki
students.role: MISSING DATA: excellent grades but the interest questionnaire was never filled. Classical logic (closed world) abstains from recommending; default logic presumes; fuzzy logic imputes a neutral interest.
students.expected: classical: eligible but NOT recommended; default: presumed recommendations; fuzzy: ranked scores

students.name: Karim Boudjema
students.role: EXCEPTION: excellent AI-related grades but a declared dislike of AI (interest 1/10). The default 'strong in algorithms => suited for AI' must be DEFEATED by this exception, while SE is recommended.
students.expected: suited_ai NOT concluded (default defeated); SE recommended

students.name: Ines Larbi
students.role: BELIEF REVISION: questionnaire missing at first (defaults presume AI aptitude), then the follow-up arrives and reveals a strong dislike of AI and a strong interest in SE. The presumed AI conclusion must be effectively RETRACTED (non-monotonicity), while classical logic keeps it (monotonicity limitation).
students.expected: phase 1: recommended_ai presumed; phase 2: recommended_ai retracted, recommended_se justified

students.name: Omar Cherif
students.role: Solid cybersecurity profile with average programming; borderline for the strict SE rule (programming 13 < 14).

students.name: Nadia Slimani
students.role: BORDERLINE everywhere: math 13 misses the crisp AI threshold by 1 point, interests and skills are 6 (< 7). Crisp logic produces threshold artefacts; fuzzy logic produces gradual scores; default logic presumes aptitude without recommending.
students.expected: classical: eligible SE only, no recommendation; default: suited_ai + suited_se presumed; fuzzy: medium scores on all majors

students.name: Riad Amrani
students.role: AMBIGUOUS PROFILE: strong everywhere with EQUAL declared interests in SE and Cybersecurity (7 = 7). Default logic represents this hesitation as TWO extensions (Nixon-diamond pattern), fuzzy logic gives close scores, classical logic recommends several majors without being able to rank them.
students.expected: 2 default extensions (oriented_se XOR oriented_cyber); all majors recommended classically
